tldr: For the population mean ATE with public Bernoulli assignment and only separately certified armwise raw-second-moment caps, the exact Gaussian-reference cost of finite-sample whole-parent honesty is \(c(s)=C(v(s),w(s),\alpha)\). A total jointly Borel connected interval family is exactly ninety-percent honest for every finite sample size and every Borel law in the parent, and attains this constant locally uniformly. A full original-record likelihood converse matches it, and a terminating rational algorithm evaluates the connected value, its ratio to the Gaussian comparator, and their difference to arbitrary precision. The Gaussian comparator is the Pratt value in its locally uniform limit; its anchored original-record rule is exactly honest and first-order attaining. Whole-parent honesty has a strictly positive additional cost for every \(0<s<1\). The diagonal-bias envelope explains the endpoint behavior: \(c(s)=\Theta(1)\) and \(c(s)/g(s)=\Theta(s^{-1/2})\) as \(s\downarrow0\), while \(c(s)/g(s)-1=O(\sqrt{1-s})\) as \(s\uparrow1\). Novelty concerns this exact problem and frontier, not the raw-moment inequality itself. Application requires public raw-square calibration about a fixed outcome origin and scale.
gap: Cai--Low is the closest conceptual comparator for honest expected length and adaptation, rather than a source of this exact raw-cap reference value. Romano--Wolf combines finite-sample validity and large-sample efficiency under known compact support. Derumigny--Girard--Guyonvarch calibrates asymptotically exact intervals under bounded kurtosis. Van Parys--Zwart studies centered-moment location classes and fixed-margin exponential rates. None supplies the entire origin-dependent raw outcome-energy parent or its unrestricted connected ATE reference-length optimum.
fill: A certified connected-action approximation is paired with a full-record likelihood converse and an unconditional finite-sample lift over the entire raw-cap parent. The exact value, optimal family, public diagonal thresholds and computable Gaussian comparison are the answer-open kernel. Scientific or administrative certification supplies the maintained raw-square bounds, with rescaling for a known common bound; unknown variance bounds, ordinary finite variance, observed-sample normalization and software promises do not supply them. The Cai--Low comparison is conceptual, with no claimed reduction or strict tightening of their published results. The Gaussian comparison starts from the genuine finite count-mixture program, whose first-order value is Pratt's scalar optimum; boundary projection, missing arms and count-dependent error allocation have vanishing scaled cost.
